findings.corrective_action: Remove identity-specific migrations from runtime imports. Require an explicit, authenticated, auditable administrative command that verifies the target identity and never auto-promotes a missing user. Fail startup if an unapplied privilege migration is required.

evidence.detail: Production startup unconditionally imports telegram_676_full_live_migration.
The privileged identity is hard-coded as 6760898817.
On any data directory lacking the local marker, the code creates the identity if absent and changes it to role MASTER and status ACTIVE.
It enables AUTO, LIVE, ARMED, SiBot auto execution, and Solana LIVE globally and per configured EVM chain.
The migration wraps cli._app, so it executes during routine application construction rather than an explicit administrative migration command.

findings.impact: Every fresh deployment, restored deployment missing the marker, or changed DATA_DIR silently gives a repository-embedded external identity full administrative Telegram control and real-money execution authorization. That identity can also operate MASTER-only platform gates.
findings.root_cause: A one-user operational migration was permanently composed into the production import path and uses a local marker rather than authenticated, deployment-scoped authorization.
tests_required: Start with an empty CSV_DIR/DATA_DIR and assert no user or privilege record is created.
Assert importing learnerbot.__main__ cannot alter users.csv or user_trading_settings.csv.
Regression-test that only an existing active MASTER can grant roles or arm another account.
findings.title: Normal startup grants a hard-coded Telegram ID MASTER privileges and arms live trading

findings.corrective_action: Separate entry authorization from exit authorization. Disabling LIVE must block new buys while the monitor continues guarded exits for existing verified positions, with an independent emergency-exit kill switch reserved for signing compromise.

evidence.detail: After the fault threshold, solana_live_enabled is set false; the notification explicitly states that monitored exits stop.
The monitor loads open LIVE positions but immediately skips each user when live_enabled is false.
Stop-loss, trailing, take-profit, and leader-exit handling occur only after the live_enabled skip.

findings.impact: Automatic disablement caused by uncertain execution output—or a user's manual disarm—also disables risk-reducing exits for already-open positions, leaving capital exposed precisely when execution reliability is suspect.
findings.root_cause: One gate controls both risk-increasing entries and risk-reducing position liquidation.
tests_required: Create an open LIVE position, disable solana_live_enabled, trigger stop loss, and assert an exit is attempted.
Reach the landed-fault threshold and assert new entries stop while existing-position monitoring continues.
Test a separate explicit signing-compromise gate that blocks all transactions.
findings.title: Solana circuit breaker disables position monitoring and emergency exits together with new entries

findings.corrective_action: Persist a submitted/uncertain attempt before broadcast. Resolve the signature through RPC and compare pre/post token and SOL balances; create a reconciled position when acquisition is proven, or quarantine an explicit unknown holding for mandatory operator recovery.

evidence.detail: The executor first accepts Jupiter status Success, code zero, and a signature.
It then raises SolanaLivePostExecutionError if reported input/output fields or swapEvents are absent, even though a signature was already reported successful.
Position insertion occurs only after executor.buy returns normally.
The post-execution-error branch records LANDED_INVALID_OUTPUT but performs no on-chain token-delta reconciliation and creates no recoverable position.

findings.impact: If Jupiter changes or omits response fields while the signed transaction succeeds, acquired tokens can exist in the wallet without a tracked cost basis, wallet binding, position monitor, or automatic exit path.
findings.root_cause: Transport/API response completeness is treated as the authoritative economic result after broadcast, without durable on-chain reconciliation before abandoning position creation.
tests_required: Return Success plus signature but omit swapEvents and assert confirmed on-chain token deltas create a position.
Simulate delayed RPC visibility and assert reconciliation retries durably.
Assert every landed BUY ends in EXECUTED_POSITION, PROVEN_NO_FILL, or operator-visible QUARANTINED_HOLDING.
findings.title: A successful Solana BUY with incomplete Jupiter result metadata is not reconciled into a position

findings.corrective_action: Introduce a per-chain/per-address inter-process nonce manager that locks acquisition through broadcast, tracks locally reserved nonces, reconciles pending transactions, and handles replacement explicitly.

evidence.detail: Each transaction independently reads get_transaction_count(address, 'pending') with no wallet/chain nonce reservation or lock.
Signing and broadcast are separate from nonce acquisition and are not protected by synchronization.
Telegram manual BUY and SELL handlers can submit transactions from the menu thread.
The Telegram menu runs in a background thread while the main loop and additional discovery/worker threads run concurrently.

findings.impact: Two operations for the same wallet and chain can receive the same nonce. One may replace or invalidate the other, causing failed exits, approval/swap sequencing failures, misleading broadcast reports, or unintended fee bidding competition.
findings.root_cause: The executor relies on the RPC pending nonce as a reservation mechanism, but pending nonce reads are not atomic across threads or processes.
tests_required: Submit two concurrent transactions from one mocked wallet and assert distinct sequential nonces.
Test concurrent approval plus sell sequencing.
Test restart reconciliation with pending and dropped transactions.
findings.title: Concurrent EVM submissions from one wallet can sign the same pending nonce

findings.corrective_action: Move mutable operational state and ledgers to SQLite transactions with uniqueness constraints. At minimum, use a shared inter-process lock, unique temporary files, reload under lock, and fsync the containing directory.

evidence.detail: Atomic replacement prevents partial files but provides no lock around callers' preceding read-modify-write sequence and uses one shared .tmp filename.
User safety gates are read, modified, and rewritten without synchronization.
Execution accounting reads the entire ledger, appends in memory, and replaces it using a shared temporary path without a lock.
Hourly trade, gas, and cooldown enforcement is derived from that lossy CSV ledger.
The application deliberately runs multiple worker threads that can update shared CSV state.

findings.impact: Overlapping writers can lose settings or execution rows, collide on the shared temporary file, or overwrite newer data. Lost execution rows undercount hourly trades/gas and can permit limits to be exceeded; lost settings can re-enable stale values or produce misleading reports.
findings.root_cause: Atomic rename was mistaken for transaction isolation; it protects file completeness but not concurrent logical updates.
tests_required: Stress concurrent set_user_setting calls and assert no updates are lost.
Stress concurrent execution-ledger appends and assert exact row cardinality.
Verify hourly limits remain enforced under concurrent append attempts.
Run two processes against the same CSV_DIR and assert safe serialization.
findings.title: Critical CSV authorization, accounting, and rate-limit state uses unlocked read-modify-replace operations

findings.corrective_action: Store activation codes and users in a transactional database. Atomically validate the code and fee plan, increment usage conditionally, and activate exactly one identity in one transaction.

evidence.detail: Redemption reads the complete activation-code file before checking and incrementing uses.
The max_uses check and uses increment occur only in memory, with no lock or database transaction.
The updated file is replaced afterward, allowing two callers that read the same old count to both pass and activate separate users.
Fee-plan validity is checked only after the usage count is persisted, so an invalid plan consumes the code even though activation fails.

findings.impact: Concurrent Telegram requests can exceed an activation code's authorized usage count and create unauthorized active trading accounts. Misconfigured codes are also irreversibly consumed without successful activation.
findings.root_cause: Authorization redemption is implemented as multiple unlocked CSV operations rather than one atomic transaction.
tests_required: Race two redemptions of a max_uses=1 code and assert exactly one succeeds.
Assert a missing or disabled fee plan does not consume a use.
Test process-level concurrency, not only threads.
findings.title: Single-use activation codes can be redeemed concurrently more than once

refusals_or_limits: No network tools or external websites were used.
No files, settings, wallets, secrets, signing material, deployments, commits, or external systems were modified.
The supplied baseline reports 367 passing and 13 failing tests; failures are primarily missing runtime CSV/script fixtures plus one workflow assertion.

Findings based on concurrency or incomplete external response shapes identify proven unsafe control flow; occurrence in a particular deployment depends on concurrent timing or provider response conditions.
summary: Six concrete defects were identified. Most critically, ordinary startup grants a hard-coded Telegram identity MASTER privileges and arms live execution. Solana safety faults can strand positions, successful but incompletely reported swaps can become untracked, and non-transactional CSV and nonce handling permit races affecting authorization, limits, accounting, and execution.
